    cost = d["cost"]
    cap = d["cap"]
    city_cap = d["city_cap"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # --- Sets -------------------------------------------------------------
    model.N = pyo.RangeSet(0, n - 1)
    # arc set: all ordered pairs of distinct cities appearing in the cost data
    model.A = pyo.Set(initialize=list(cost.keys()), dimen=2)

    # --- Variables --------------------------------------------------------
    def x_bounds(m, i, j):
        # link capacity: 0 <= x[i,j] <= cap[i,j]
        return (0, cap[(i, j)])

    model.x = pyo.Var(model.A, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=x_bounds)

    # --- Objective: minimise total transportation cost --------------------
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(cost[(i, j)] * m.x[i, j] for (i, j) in m.A)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # --- Constraints ------------------------------------------------------
    # Flow balance: inflow - outflow = net_supply[i]
    # (equivalently inflow + supply = outflow + demand)
    def balance_rule(m, i):
        inflow = sum(m.x[j, i] for (j, k) in m.A if k == i)
        outflow = sum(m.x[i, j] for (k, j) in m.A if k == i)
        return inflow - outflow == net_supply[i]

    model.balance = pyo.Constraint(model.N, rule=balance_rule)

    # City capacity: total inflow into a city <= city_cap[i]
    def citycap_rule(m, i):
        return sum(m.x[j, i] for (j, k) in m.A if k == i) <= city_cap[i]

    model.citycap = pyo.Constraint(model.N, rule=citycap_rule)

    return model
